from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 7  # sources
    J = 6  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [206, 166, 141, 120, 243, 207, 183]
    demands = [22, 12, 49, 16, 18, 26]
    cost_matrix = [[7.87, 15.23, 11.92, 13.05, 7.66, 27.5], [22.45, 26.01, 3.8, 19.93, 24.59, 17.35], [29.31, 10.47, 12.25, 29.58, 6.63, 9.67], [26.71, 22.55, 6.35, 11.4, 20.35, 3.17], [25.26, 13.19, 12.37, 3.32, 12.06, 24.4], [5.0, 13.12, 5.65, 10.99, 16.02, 17.32], [11.68, 17.06, 4.12, 3.24, 3.66, 16.25]]
    emission_matrix = [[9.15, 16.85, 13.84, 5.79, 8.69, 14.17], [9.48, 11.21, 17.48, 8.73, 17.88, 10.25], [9.3, 8.03, 18.72, 16.57, 15.37, 3.23], [15.93, 9.49, 15.46, 7.86, 5.17, 8.67], [3.79, 6.97, 5.55, 20.0, 19.6, 11.75], [7.84, 12.85, 4.55, 18.93, 1.0, 7.31], [7.39, 4.66, 10.45, 18.32, 12.15, 15.48]]
    fixed_costs = [[112, 138, 146, 207, 144, 134], [141, 274, 211, 180, 109, 163], [174, 75, 101, 255, 71, 226], [297, 259, 114, 58, 84, 89], [156, 283, 178, 251, 183, 179], [50, 178, 69, 181, 222, 208], [254, 272, 109, 205, 228, 99]]
    moq = [[6, 12, 14, 11, 10, 16], [12, 10, 12, 16, 16, 14], [12, 19, 20, 19, 11, 14], [15, 20, 10, 8, 9, 9], [10, 18, 10, 12, 14, 16], [6, 13, 6, 10, 12, 11], [16, 14, 5, 12, 18, 5]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Executive Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Subject: Balanced shipping plan for warehouse-to-store deliveries
Date:

Context
We ship from multiple warehouses to a network of stores. Each possible route is measured on both monetary cost per unit and the carbon emission rate per unit. In practice, the most economical routes often carry a higher carbon footprint, while cleaner options can be more expensive. We need to balance financial discipline with our sustainability commitments while maintaining reliable service to every store.

Operational rules and real-world considerations
- Route setup/activation: Using any new warehouse-to-store route triggers a one-time setup expense for contracts, compliance, and dock readiness. This charge applies in full as soon as the route is used, regardless of how much we ship on it.
- Minimum order quantities: Once a route is activated, we must ship at least the route’s defined minimum volume to justify equipment, loading, and transportation requirements. Partial truckloads are not accepted on these lanes.
- Supplier limits per store: For receiving dock capacity and vendor management practicality, each store can be served by only a limited number of warehouses. This cap simplifies inbound scheduling and reduces complexity at the store.

Supply and demand
Any plan must respect warehouse inventory availability and ensure each store’s minimum demand is met. We will not over-allocate from any warehouse, and we will not under-serve any store.

Management priority
Leadership has set relative importance weights for costs and emissions. We will evaluate candidate shipping plans using a combined score that applies the agreed weights to the per-unit variable shipping spend and to total emissions. In addition, the one-time route setup charges are added in full; they are not subject to those weights.

Business goal
Our goal is to identify which routes to activate and how much to ship on each route such that:
- Warehouse inventory is not exceeded
- Every store’s demand requirement is satisfied
- Activated routes meet their minimum order commitment
- Each store is served by no more than the allowed number of warehouses
- The combined score—weighted variable cost and emissions plus full route setup costs—is as low as possible

Next steps
We will generate a recommended routing plan that specifies:
- Which routes to activate
- Shipment quantities by route
- Expected spend and emissions under the combined score
We will also highlight key trade-offs and provide scenario views if management wishes to shift the relative importance of cost versus emissions or adjust operational limits.
